title: 2D Isometric RPG, agentic workflow and art assets
author: MF2D
selftext:
Hi! Last weekend I decided to design a game for funsies and I’m having a blast. I use VS code/Claude code daily for work and had a concept for a game and said fuck it - why not? 

Initial setup was Claude/godot with placeholders for art until I had a basic main area and npcs, game logic, dialog,etc. I had Claude generate an art pipeline and handoff markdown for ChatGPT to reference from GitHub. Had it create a few characters sheets and building art. 

Then I ran into issues w token consumption as Claude was having to tweak the art to fit or make adjustments every batch. Eventually with the npcs and player sheets it got to the point where the sheets work every time and animations look crisp. 

I ended up using codex only for the art gen bit in VSCode. Seemed to be much smoother. The buildings and other art work immediately with no back and forth. 

My question is; how can I improve this process? Is there a better tool/service for generating art assets?

Thank you.

comments.author: waypostmaster
comments.body: You could try plausibleventures/lattice; not sure if it will do what you want.

comments.author: GrowByDate
comments.body:
I think you're probably doing better than most having usable sheets.

I'm at the point where I'm thinking about using my concept images to make my own timesheets because I haven't found a process that's not frustrating.

I heard Astra is better with computer use for making pixel art on screen but that seems like a buggy process too.  Computer use in Codex doesn't work on Windows 10 (yes I know, that's my problem) and when I finally setup CLI in aseprite the results were less than promising.

replies.author: MF2D
replies.body:
I’m thinking about playing around pixellab + aseprite on the free trial today. 

I tried astra yesterday w codex for building out some of the roofing and while it worked well the usage was insane. Sol seems to do ok but a bit more finicky. 

Long term right now I’m concerned with continuity and degradation over time. It hasn’t been an issue yet but I’m still experimenting

comments.author: Corwar
comments.body:
i have great success with référence key pose image from web into imagegen 2 with my character then asesprite edit via mcp to remove any drift in design or character proposition. i run everything on gpt6 high and the result is excellent. 

i also have some written art direction for vfx and use the good vfx that has been generated as ref. 

consume all my 5h allowance in 1h but the result is worth it

comments.author: Edig50
comments.body:
We are not having problems making the art, we are having problems animating it, only if its legs and arms. I’m making a game without npc and I can do all the art with codex.

Right know I’m experimenting with aesprite and codex and it animates really good.

comments.author: Pure-Masterpiece-857
comments.body: generate 3d models then render them to a fixed perspective, then use them as input either for your asset pipeline or probably a normal deterministic pipeline. agents are just not going to get this shit right.

comments.author: Useful_Use_6170
comments.body: Right now I been testing with spritecook and pixel lab MCP still hard time deciding because they each do certain jobs better than the other, I will admit pixel labs does give you more credit for your buck!!
